content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in early cycles and underperform in late cycles.", "Sentiment spikes correlate with price overshoots, especially when positive sentiment precedes a sharp decline.", "Model bias toward higher prices persists despite historical mean-reversion signals.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment aligns with recent price trends rather than isolated spikes.", "Lagging sentiment indicators better predict price corrections than leading sentiment signals.", "Models exhibit diminishing predictive power as price volatility increases beyond 5% from recent highs.", "Price corrections often occur after model forecasts peak, suggesting a lagged reaction to sentiment shifts.", "Sentiment-driven price reversals are more likely when forecasted peaks are followed by negative sentiment."]}
